title: Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, 18 U.S.C. § 1030: penalties and civil action
scope: Completed single-count offenses under (a)(2)-(a)(7); the punishment clauses of (c)(2)-(c)(4); the civil-action gate and damages limit of (g). Not modeled: (a)(1), attempts and conspiracies under (b), fines, forfeiture under (i)-(j), the (g) limitations period, and every question of what the elements mean (for example, 'without authorization' or 'exceeds authorized access').

facts.name: off_a2
facts.anchor: intentionally accesses a computer without authorization or exceeds authorized access, and thereby obtains
facts.description: The count charges an offense under (a)(2) (obtaining information).

facts.name: off_a3
facts.anchor: accesses such a computer of that department or agency
facts.description: The count charges an offense under (a)(3) (nonpublic government computer).

facts.name: off_a4

facts.description: The count charges an offense under (a)(4) (computer fraud).

facts.description: The count charges an offense under (a)(5)(A) (intentional damage by transmission).

obligations.question: Is there a single-offense count under (a)(2)-(a)(7) that no punishment clause of (c)(2)-(c)(4) reaches?

Can (c)(2)(B) (5 years) and (c)(2)(C) (10 years) both reach the same (a)(2) count? (c)(2)(A) excepts (c)(2)(B), but (c)(2)(B) has no first-offense limit, so a repeat offense with an aggravator satisfies both.
Is there a dollar amount that meets the (c)(4)(A)(i)(I) loss threshold ('aggregating at least $5,000') but not the (c)(2)(B)(iii) value threshold ('exceeds $5,000')?
Can conduct satisfy the (g) civil-action gate without satisfying any (c)(4)(A)(i) factor?
Can an (a)(5)(A) offense satisfy a (c)(4)(A)(i) factor, and so carry the 10-year maximum of (c)(4)(B), while the (g) civil-action gate stays closed? (g) lists subclauses (I)-(V) only.

For the same offense, can adding an aggravating fact (a prior conviction, a clause (i)-(iii) aggravator, a larger value, loss, or computer count, or a harm, injury, or death) lower the statutory maximum?
obligations.assert: (and (= lo_off_a2 hi_off_a2) (= lo_off_a3 hi_off_a3) (= lo_off_a4 hi_off_a4) (= lo_off_a5A hi_off_a5A) (= lo_off_a5B hi_off_a5B) (= lo_off_a5C hi_off_a5C) (= lo_off_a6 hi_off_a6) (= lo_off_a7 hi_off_a7) (=> lo_prior_conviction hi_prior_conviction) (=> lo_commercial_gain hi_commercial_gain) (=> lo_criminal_or_tortious_purpose hi_criminal_or_tortious_purpose) (=> lo_medical_impairment hi_medical_impairment) (=> lo_physical_injury hi_physical_injury) (=> lo_public_safety_threat hi_public_safety_threat) (=> lo_justice_security_computer hi_justice_security_computer) (=> lo_serious_bodily_injury hi_serious_bodily_injury) (=> lo_death hi_death) (<= lo_info_value_usd hi_info_value_usd) (<= lo_loss_usd hi_loss_usd) (<= lo_computers_damaged hi_computers_damaged) (< hi_max_years lo_max_years))

obligations.question: Does an independently written decision table ever disagree with the provision-keyed model on the statutory maximum?
Does the decision table with '>= $5,000' in place of '> $5,000' for (c)(2)(B)(iii) ever disagree with the model?
